Alex: hey folks — I have a small PR that touches routing fallback + auth header ordering and I'd like runtime/infra/security eyes before we merge in tonight's slot. PR: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/63190 :eyes:
Alex: TL;DR: swaps precedence of x-routing-precedence and x-authz to avoid double-eval in some paths. unit tests added, integration flaky only on one env. hoping for quick async sign-off or a short mitigation suggestion. @Sam @Priya @Jamie
Sam: can take a look in ~25m, tagging in perf bench run. quick q — does this change affect KV cache keying?
Alex: no KV key changes, only header order and a tiny guard in router.go. added this test: `TestRoutingHeaderPrecedence` to ensure deterministic behaviour.
Priya: security quick note: header reorder can affect authz bypass if legacy clients send both headers. need to confirm behavior for unparsable auth tokens. can you paste the guard logic? :mag:
Alex: sure — snippet below:
```
if headers.Has("x-routing-precedence") {
  useRoutingPriority()
} else if headers.Has("x-authz") {
  enforceAuthz()
}
```
Alex: fallback keeps previous path if neither present. I added extra logging on parse error.
Jamie: infra: I don't see infra-level risk. main ask is please run short perf run — header parsing happens on hot path. Sam - can you include this in your bench?
Sam: yes, will run bench for 2 min and post numbers. if +<3% token path latency we should still be fine for tonight's slot.
Priya: security: if parse error leads to skip authz we need fail-closed. small suggestion: change enforceAuthz() to return error on malformed token and reject upstream request. if you can wire that quick, i'll sign off.
Alex: good catch. swapping to fail-closed is trivial — I'll push a tiny fix now and ping.
ci-bot: CI: build/presubmit passed for PR #63190 — 7 checks green.
Alex: pushed fix — changed to fail-closed and updated test to cover malformed token case. https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/63190/files
Sam: bench results: baseline median p50=12.1ms, new p50=12.8ms (+5.7%). p99 unchanged. I think within acceptable bounds but marking for canary routing to be safe.
Jamie: agree. schedule canary for low-traffic window (02:00 PT) and monitor token-latency metric. I'll reserve the slot.
Priya: security LGTm after fail-closed change. add a short note to the release doc about backward-compat concern for old clients.
Alex: thanks all. plan: merge after Jamie confirms canary slot reserved, then roll canary 02:00 PT, watch token-latency and auth-failure-rate for 10m. I'll DM if anything odd. :thumbsup:
Jamie: slot reserved. ping if you want me to coordinate rollback.
Sam: lgtm from perf side for canary.
Priya: lgtm from security.
Alex: merging in 10m unless anyone shouts. thanks! :pray:
